meaning:
πόλεμος, -ον, ό
[in LXX chiefly for מִלְחָמָה ;]
1. war: Mat.24:6, Mrk.13:7, Luk.14:31 21:9, Heb.11:34; π. ποιεῖν, before μετά, with genitive (cf. πολεμέω), Rev.11:7 12:17 13:7 19:19.
2. = μάχη, a fight, battle: 1Co.14:8, Rev.9:7, 9 12:7 16:14 20:8; hyperb., of private quarrels (cf. πολεμέω), Jas.4:1.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you aren’t troubled, for all this must happen, but the end is not yet.
“When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.
Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes…
For if the trumpet gave an uncertain sound, who would prepare himself for war?
quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, from weakness were made strong, grew mighty in war, and caused foreign armies to flee.
Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members?
The shapes of the locusts were like horses prepared for war. On their heads were something like golden crowns, and their faces were like people’s faces.
